questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether an Affine Transformation is Orientation-Preserving
questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2v-u+2,\,y=2u+v-5.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-5$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is true. Indeed, notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2v-u+2 \\ 2u+v-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+2v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|=(-1)\cdot 1-2\cdot 2=-5.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $det(A)<0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is not orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether an Affine Transformation is Orientation-Preserving
questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=4u-3v-5,\,y=-2u+2v+4.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=2$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4u-3v-5 \\ -2u+2v+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u-3v \\ -2u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is true. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}|=4\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-2)=2.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $det(A)>0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14056028/assets/43eb119ef43e136682d4451e4f85f007c63568f7a34880c46f87ab45122f5dd0.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=1-u,\,y=2-v.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-u \\ 2-v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u \\ -v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14056028/assets/a8a13c579c3ca8cc32f997c48e237c38d449aa07040de658589fa5cc68a02c55.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(2,2),(-1,2),(-1,1),$ and $(2,1).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14056028/assets/146f9f36deeac0f3a7108a173485eb6d0d03138d18998a96dc9c3566bee21ca2.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=1>0,$ this transformation is orientation-preserving.

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=u+v-2,\,y=u-3v+1.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v-2 \\ u-3v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|=1\cdot (-3)-1\cdot 1=-4.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|-4|=4.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=2u-v,\,y=2v-u-5.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ 2v-u-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ -u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|=2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-1)=3.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|3|=3.
$$
